transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, what really scared me enough to actually make an appointment is... I just keep thinking it would be so much easier if I just didn't wake up. It's been happening a lot lately. And sometimes, when I'm driving home from the clinic, I actually catch myself wondering what would happen if I just didn't turn the wheel. It frightened me to realize I was thinking that way, so I knew I needed to come in.
Have you experienced a period of feeling this way, or having these types of thoughts, at any point in your life before now?

No... I really haven't. I mean, I've never had thoughts like this before, about just not waking up or crashing my car. It's never crossed my mind in the past, which is why it scared me so much this time.
Have you been hearing, seeing, or sensing things that other people around you do not seem to notice?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I haven't heard or seen anything that isn't really there. It's really just those thoughts I mentioned... but no, nothing unusual like what you're asking about.
Are you currently able to perform your daily tasks, such as going to work or taking care of your basic needs, or have you become unable to function in these areas?

Honestly, I'm really struggling right now. I'm still going to work, but I've... I've started making mistakes at the clinic, which is terrifying. Outside of work, I'm just avoiding my friends completely because I'm so afraid I'll either snap at someone or just fall apart. And at home... my husband has basically had to take over everything. He's paying the bills, making the meals, and just... trying to keep me safe when those dark thoughts happen. So, no, I'm not really keeping up with my normal tasks at all.

Have you been experiencing any fixed, false beliefs—for instance, do you feel like you are being watched, or do you have a strong, persistent feeling that you have committed an unforgivable sin or that you have lost all your money, even if those things aren't true?

No, nothing like that. I don't feel like I'm being watched or followed, and I know our finances are fine. I haven't had any strange beliefs like that... just the overwhelming sadness and the thoughts I told you about. But my grip on reality is still there.
Have you noticed any physical changes, such as your movements feeling significantly slower than usual, or perhaps a sense of restlessness that makes it hard for you to sit still?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't feel restless, and I'm not having any trouble sitting still. And I don't think my movements are any slower than usual, either. Physically, I feel like I'm moving normally... it's just the mental part that's so heavy right now.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your ability to sleep since you started feeling this way?

Well, my appetite has been all over the place. Lately, I mostly just pick at some toast or have a cup of coffee... and then I'll get to the end of a clinic shift and realize that I’ve barely eaten anything all day. I haven't really noticed a major change with my sleep, but I'm definitely not eating like I normally do.
Do you find that you are still able to enjoy the things you used to love, or does it feel like you have lost the ability to feel pleasure or happiness in almost everything you do?

No, I really can't say I'm enjoying much of anything lately. It's... it's actually kind of frightening. I haven't even touched my camera in weeks. Usually, I love photography, and I'd be out checking the bird feeders or seeing what's coming up in the garden, but... I just don't have any interest in it right now. I don't really care about any of it. And that's hard, because those things used to be how I felt like myself. Now, it just feels like that ability to feel happy about them is completely gone.
Have your friends or family mentioned that you seem to be moving or speaking much more slowly than usual, or that you seem 'shut down' in a way that they can clearly see?

No, no one has mentioned anything like that. My husband hasn't said anything, and the people I work with at the clinic haven't either. Like I was saying before, I really think I'm moving and talking at my normal pace. I don't think I look shut down from the outside... it's really just how heavy everything feels on the inside.
